facts.text: Weinland Park takes its name from City Councilman Edgar Weinland, a reformer who helped secure the park space in the 1920s.
The neighborhood grew in the 1930s and 1940s when streetcar lines and nearby factories drew working and middle‑class families.
Recent upgrades include a new Weinland Park Elementary School, the Schoenbaum Family Center, a police sub‑station, a Kroger, and the South Campus Gateway.
When Ohio State was founded in 1870, the area that is now Weinland Park was still open farmland.
Weinland Park stretches roughly 217 acres, bounded by Chittenden Avenue, Fifth Avenue, the railroad tracks, and North High Street.
The neighborhood was first platted in 1916 as “New Indianola” and designed as a streetcar suburb by developer Charles Johnson.
